body:
PR #266 (`claude/cap-lifetime`, team-fix) has run its 4 audit rounds without converging. Under rule 02 it stays a draft until the owner rules here.

## Rounds

| Round | Head | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 32c94f5 | complete; 9 in-diff (all fixed), 4 pre-existing |
| 2 | 19271ae | complete; 4 in-diff (all fixed) |
| 3 | 22d4897 | complete; 7 in-diff (all fixed or answered), 1 pre-existing |
| 4 | 498699b | complete; **1 in-diff (nit)**, 2 pre-existing |

Each round file is in `.git/aios-agent/audit/claude-cap-lifetime/<head>.json`. Round 4 used base 4cbb812, the merge-base after main's #257.

## Open finding (round 4, in-diff, nit, 1 of 1 skeptics confirmed)

- **File:** `docs/platform/linux-compat/syscall-translation.md:140-141`
- **Finding:** the file still maps `wait4` and `waitid` (P_PID / P_PGID / P_ALL) to `ProcessWait`. #266 changed `docs/platform/posix.md:659` and `docs/kernel/ipc.md` §3.1 to say that `ProcessWait` takes one child pid and has no wait-any form, so the three docs now disagree.
- **Proposed fix (doc-writer, docs only):** note on both rows that `ProcessWait` serves only a known child pid (P_PID). P_PGID, P_ALL and `wait4(-1)` stay unsupported until a wait-any primitive exists.

## Pre-existing (not for #266; recorded in #268)

- The echo demo exits pid 7 outside the interim exit rule (`kernel/src/service/mod.rs:365`). This is new to #268: https://github.com/juslee/aios/issues/268#issuecomment-6435852771
- The stale request left in the ring after a timed-out call (`kernel/src/ipc/channel.rs:221`). This is already a #268 item.

## Gates on 498699b

- **Build and tests:** build 0 warnings; `just check` passes; 793 tests pass; the tools gates pass.
- **docs-check:** only the 2 scheduled items, the developer-guide count and the plan's presence.
- **Gate boot** `cap-lifetime-merge-4cbb812-1`: CLEAN. Every self-test passes, `latereply=0`, and there is no new WARN text.
- **CI:** everything passes except "Security (audit + deny)", which fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (ctutils 0.4.2 through aes-gcm). That failure hits every PR and will hit main, and team-build has raised it with the owner.

## Owner decision needed

1. **Accept the nit fix without a fifth round** (recommended). doc-writer applies the fix above, the lead fast-forwards it, and the PR moves on to the soak pair, step 16 and the ship pass.
2. **Allow a fifth audit round** on the fix head.
3. **Waive the nit.** The fix moves to #268 or a later docs PR.
title: Gate: PR #266 audit did not converge

body:
## Purpose

This issue tracks pre-existing IPC and scheduler bugs found during the capability-lifetime work (#266) that #266 does not fix. It replaces one issue per finding: new findings of this kind go here as a checklist item, and in the plan's "Issues Encountered".

Every item below is pre-existing on `main`, was found by a Fable review and confirmed by a skeptic, and is **latent today**: no boot path reaches it.

## Items

- [ ] **Stale request left in the ring after a timed-out call** (was #265). **Owner decision needed.**
  1. An `ipc_call` that exits on timeout, cancel or EPIPE leaves its request queued.
  2. The server later pops that request.
  3. Its `ipc_reply` claims whichever call is pending at that moment, so that call receives the answer to a request it never sent.

  The fix options trade off differently:
  - (a) remove the caller's own request on the error exit. This only narrows the window: the server may already have popped it;
  - (b) carry a request id through `ipc_recv`/`ipc_reply` (an API change). A candidate design, 777d883, was written during #266 step 14 and is not merged; it is described in the #265 comment;
  - (c) serialise calls per channel.
- [ ] **`process_exit` drops EPIPE wakes past 16** (was #262). `exit_channels` collects at most 16 waiters into `epipe_wakeups`. Any further waiters have already been taken out of their channels, so they stay Blocked forever (scan B reports `nowaker`). Fix: size the array `2 * MAX_CHANNELS`, or count first. Separately, `ResourceLimits.max_channels` is not enforced.
- [ ] **The direct switch and the reply switch ignore the target's CPU affinity** (was #258). `try_direct_switch` and `try_reply_switch` run the target on the current CPU without checking its `CpuSet`.

## Related, still open separately

- #253: IPC receive-path panics on CI (crash-fix H1).
- #236: scan A holds every run queue plus THREAD_TABLE in CPU 0's IRQ (crash-fix).
- #187: unchecked tid indexing (partly fixed by #266).
- #190: Kit errno mapping (partly fixed by #266).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Routine commands from the PR #234 harness have no allow rule, so they prompt in attended sessions and are refused in `-p` or background runs. This is an owner decision: keep each as a deliberate ask, or add a narrow allow (never a broad `*` form that hides a command-running option; see #242's `git branch *` and the `git ls-remote --upload-pack` lesson).

| Who | Commands |
|---|---|
| lead | `git -C <W> merge --ff-only worktree-*`, `git -C <W> rev-list --first-parent …`, `git -C <W> branch -d worktree-*`, `git -C <W> push -u origin claude/<branch>` (Q6 chose literal-path rules in `.claude/settings.local.json`; `docs/project/agent-loop.md` lists them) |
| worker | `shellcheck <files>`, `actionlint <files>` |
| verifier | `git archive`, `kill -TERM <pid>` (stopping its own lock run), `python3` (the A/B Fisher test), `"$(rustc --print sysroot)"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-objdump -h …` |

Also from #234: in auto mode the classifier refuses agents' Write of `.claude/settings.json`, `git rm` of hook files and the commit that carries them ("Self-Modification"); the owner ran those steps. Plan settings/hook changes as owner-run steps.
title: settings: decide allow rules for routine lead, worker and verifier commands (from #234)

body:
Follow-up to #184 D04. On `claude/docs-update-184-arch-inconsistencies`, the D04 commit (`cb48d9e`) and audit rounds 1–3 (`fc2b9e5`, `04ca012`, `aaf143a`) mapped every number that has a §8 row and added "no §8 row" notes for the rest. This issue lists the drift still there at branch head `aaf143a`. On main (`7334601`) none of D04 is fixed yet.

Paths are relative to `docs/`. `project/development-plan.md` §8 is authoritative and is the same on main and the branch.

Items 1–4 wait on an owner decision, hence `needs-human`. Items 5–6 need no decision and are open to agents.

## Owner decisions (no §8 row)

These are #184's "D04 (unassigned part)". The branch only adds notes for them.

1. **AIRS sub-phases.** `intelligence/airs.md:168` (14b), `:170-173` (22a, 22b, 22b+, 22c). There is a note at `:176`.
2. **Adversarial defense.** `security/adversarial-defense.md:69`, `:72`, `:82` (14b), and `:70` ("adversarial protection follows 14b"). Two rows reuse §8 numbers for different work:
   - `:86` uses 14 for semantic injection detection, but §8 14 is the Context Engine.
   - `:88` uses 39 for formal verification, but §8 39 is Secure Boot & Update System.

   There is a note at `:53`. `intelligence/intent-verifier.md:74` also points at the unscheduled 14b.
3. **Preference behavioral intelligence and full NLU.** `intelligence/preferences.md:160` uses Phase 18 (§8: Conversation Manager) and `:175` uses Phase 30 (§8: WiFi Stack). There is a note at `:140`.
4. **Formal verification has five phase numbers, and none is a §8 home:**
   - `intelligence/behavioral-monitor.md:219` reads `**34** (Secure Boot & Updates)`. In §8, 34 is Interface Kit (`project/development-plan.md:451`) and Secure Boot & Update System is 39 (`:456`). The row puts a §8-style name next to the wrong number, and the file has no "no §8 row" note, so it reads as already aligned. #184's own D04 list says 34→39, but its unassigned part lists this row as having no §8 home.
   - `security/adversarial-defense.md:88` says 39.
   - `security/adversarial-defense/testing.md:130` and `:174` say "Phase 40, which introduces static analysis and formal verification tooling". In §8, 40 is the Linux Binary Loader (`:457`). These are the same §13.4 properties that the parent doc schedules at 39, and there is no note.
   - Outside #184's list, the security docs put TLA+ at Phase 18 (§8: Conversation Manager) and Coq/Verus at Phase 35 (§8: Browser Kit):
     - Phase 18: `security/model.md:113`, `security/model/hardening.md:362`, `security/model/operations.md:443` and `:456-457`, `security/fuzzing/adoption-roadmap.md:130`, `security/static-analysis.md:200` and `:246`.
     - Phase 35: `security/fuzzing.md:17`, `security/fuzzing/adoption-roadmap.md:124` and `:130`, `security/model/hardening.md:362`, `security/model/operations.md:443`, `security/static-analysis.md:190` and `:202`.
     - `hardening.md:362` reads "TLA+ models begin in Phase 18 (Security Architecture)". Like `behavioral-monitor.md:219`, it puts a §8 name next to the wrong number: §8 18 is Conversation Manager, and Security Architecture is 21 (`project/development-plan.md:438`).
   - Candidates: §8 22, Security Testing & Verification (`:439`), whose architecture doc `fuzzing.md` already owns the formal-verification roadmap (adoption-roadmap §4.7); or 39, as behavioral-monitor.md implies.

## Mechanical leftovers (no decision needed)

5. `security/adversarial-defense.md:4`: the header reads `**Phase:** 13b (Agent Framework — Adversarial Defense + hint screening)`. The same file's §16 calls this work 14b (`:69`), and §8 has Agent Framework as Phase 10 (`:427`). #184 cited only `:60-85`, so neither the D04 commit nor the audit rounds touched the header.
6. **Dangling 14a/14c labels.** The branch replaced the old sub-phase labels in `airs.md` §12 and `adversarial-defense.md` §16:
   - 14a (Intent Verifier + Behavioral Monitor) became 12/20.
   - 14c (Tool Manager + Agent Lifecycle) became 12.

   These lines still cite the old labels:
   - `security/adversarial-defense/threat-model.md:98` (IntentVerifier "Phase 14a")
   - `intelligence/tool-manager.md:144` and `:176` ("Dev Phase 14c")
   - `intelligence/conversation-manager.md:335` ("Dev Phase 14c")
   - `applications/agents.md:201` (Tool Manager "Phase 14c")

   The implementation-order sections in tool-manager.md and conversation-manager.md use the old plan throughout. For example, the `tool-manager.md:170-180` flowchart has "Phase 9 Agent Model", "Phase 11 AIRS Services" and "Phase 15 Task Manager".

The same kind of pre-§8 sub-phase label also appears in places #184 never listed:
- `intelligence/context-engine.md:134` and `:143` (22a, 22b).
- `storage/spaces.md:137-142`: 13c Space Sync (§8 42 is Multi-Device Sync), 18a per-space encryption (§8.2 puts it in 21), 22a–22d.
- `intelligence/space-indexer.md:153` and `:160` (11a+, 11b: search integration and entity extraction, but §8 11 is the AIRS Inference Engine), and `:179` (22+).
- `experience/experience.md:868` (13b Conversation Bar; §8 13 is Space Indexer & Search).

## Why it matters

§8 is the schedule that phase docs are generated from (`CLAUDE.md`, Phase Doc Generation Workflow step 1, and the `/generate-phase-doc` skill). A note saying "no §8 row" keeps readers from being misled, but it puts the work on no phase's plan. As a result:
- When the Phase 12, 20, 22 or 39 docs are written, adversarial defense, model residency and formal verification will be dropped or misplaced.
- Item 4's first row, `hardening.md:362` and item 5 send readers to the wrong phase today, with no note to warn them.

## Suggested fix

- Items 5–6: map the numbers to §8 as `airs.md` §12 now does. They can go in the #184 PR before it merges, or in a `claude/docs-update-*` follow-up.
- Items 1–4: the owner picks a §8 home for each, or adds §8 rows or §8.2 cross-cutting entries. Then replace each number with `N (§8 name)` and remove the notes.
- Item 4: until the owner decides, at least add a "no §8 row" note to `behavioral-monitor.md:219` and `testing.md:130`, so they agree with `adversarial-defense.md:53`.

## Found in

- #184, D04 and its unchecked "D04 (unassigned part)" item.
- Branch `claude/docs-update-184-arch-inconsistencies` at `aaf143a`. Commit `cb48d9e` says "Left for the owner (no §8 row): … formal verification (behavioral-monitor.md 34, adversarial-defense.md 39, testing.md)". `cb48d9e` and audit rounds `fc2b9e5` and `04ca012` added the notes. Items 5–6 came from re-checking that branch head against §8.

This issue was filed from a Claude Code session.

title: docs: leftover D04 phase drift after #184 (unscheduled sub-phases, formal verification, dangling 14a/14c refs)

## Decision recorded, gate open

PR #149 (Phase 7 M26: Desktop Shell) merges **only after the boot-crash fix validates on it** (owner decision, 2026-09-17). This issue tracks that gate and the work left before merge, so the PR is not merged early and nothing is forgotten.

## Context

- M26 fails 10/10 QEMU boots with the same PC=0 signature as `main` (see #164, crash-fix ADR). It amplifies the existing race; it did not introduce it.
- GitHub shows #149 as mergeable with green checks, but CI never boots QEMU, so that says nothing about bootability.
- #149's branch predates the 2026-09-22 dependency merges on `main` (now 14ff791, toolchain nightly-2026-09-17).

## Work before merge

1. Rebase `claude/phase-7-m26-desktop-shell` onto current `main` (keep both sides; `cargo metadata --locked`, `just check`, `just test`).
2. Fix the new clippy `needless_range_loop` in `kernel/src/compositor/shell/workspace.rs:557` (appears with nightly-2026-09-17).
3. Doc fixes in the same PR: M26 checkboxes and Status in `docs/phases/07-window-compositor-and-shell.md`, README status, the development-plan §8.1 row, and lock entries in `docs/kernel/deadlock-prevention.md` §3.3 and the CLAUDE.md lock order for any new shell locks. `just docs-check` should report no new drift.
4. After the crash fix (#164) is on `main`: merge `main` into the branch and soak it with the soak harness.

## Decision needed from you

Confirm the soak threshold that opens the gate:

- **A.** All boots CLEAN in 10 text-mode + 10 gpu-mode boots (about 25 minutes).
- **B.** All boots CLEAN in 20 + 20 boots (about 50 minutes; tighter bound on a residual crash rate).

Comment **A** or **B**. The agent reports soak results here; you merge #149 (the agent never merges) and close this issue.
title: Gate: merge PR #149 (Phase 7 M26) only after the boot-crash fix validates on it
